rationale: The Old English lemma *Sceáp-íg* is a place-name compound meaning "sheep island" (sceáp = sheep + íg = island), referring to a literal, concrete location associated with sheep as animals. The attestations in the Chronicle (Chr. 855) confirm this is a toponym grounded in the physical presence of woolly ruminant animals, making the literal zoological sense (sheep.n.01) the only appropriate match.
